question: What is printed in the boxed bar on that staff?
note: Sean numbered tiles 7, 8, 9 as '5, 6, 7' after tile 6 (our reading, by content). 10-12 not yet answered.
overall: many of these are taller than the tiles that you're giving me. And it's very possible that one of the reasons these are showing up as red is because of how spread out the notes are and how far away they are from the staff.

answers.1: a chord on an eighth note on beat 1, two notes, the second space above the staff and the third line above the staff, followed by three eighth notes on a beam that are also unison, so the stems going in both directions; all three on the fourth ledger line above the staff
answers.2: two half notes on a chord with a tremolo slash; stem down; notes on the first space above the staff and the fourth ledger line above the staff
answers.3: a quarter note followed by a quarter note rest; a forte on the quarter note; above it an SF that belongs to the system above, written so low it is bleeding into the staff; a very simple measure
answers.4: just a unison half note with ties on either side
answers.5: two-voice measure; bottom voice a whole note rest; top voice a natural sign in front of a half note, third space above the staff; pianissimo written in the middle of the staff belonging to the top-voice note
answers.6: a chord of two notes, first ledger line below the staff and second space within the staff, followed by a quarter note rest; fermata over the rest; a sharp in front of the note on the first ledger line below; a forte marking
answers.7: two dotted quarter notes; the first has a tie coming from the measure before, the second a tie going to the measure after
answers.8: a chord of quarter notes, middle line and the line above (flat in front), then an eighth note rest, then another chord of dotted quarters, ledger line below the staff (sharp) and middle of the staff (flat); 'piu' and a forte underneath
answers.9: two voices; top: quarter rest, eighth rest, quarter note slurred to an eighth note; bottom: two dotted quarters, the first with an arc coming from the bar before, and a slur from it to the first note of the next bar; two hairpins (decrescendo on the first dotted quarter, crescendo on the second); 'espr.' over the second half
